Preserved as printed per the diplomatic rule. ⚠ The authority field first cited Smyth §163 for this, which is wrong and was caught in adversarial review (Grok, 2026-08-08): §163 limits how far back the accent may stand, and says nothing against a first-declension oxytone — τιμή, τιμήν are perfectly legal. entries.authority: John read the 400dpi crop and confirmed an accent on the initial alpha AND on the omega. Aristotle has ἀνθρώπου, single accent, at HA 497b32 — the very passage Bonitz cites two lines later (Ζιβ1. 497 b33). An enclitic would add an acute to the ULTIMA (Smyth §183, ἄνθρωπός τις); this second accent is on the penult, adjacent to the first, which no rule permits. So the compositor doubled it. entries.rule: accent internal-consistency (Bonitz against himself)
entries.authority: An articular infinitive takes the genitive article τοῦ, which carries the circumflex — ἡ τοῦ λέγειν πιθανότης, "the persuasiveness of speaking". τοὺ with a grave is not a Greek word at all. Bonitz himself sets τȣ͂ 467 times in this corpus and τȣ̀ exactly once, here. The accusative plural τȣ̀ς is a real word and appears 178 times, including on line 32 immediately above; the two are not being confused.
entries.note: ⚠ FOUND BY THE ONE INSTRUMENT THAT COULD REACH IT. page-063-L is in both cold models' TRAINING set, so they reproduce this line from memory and can never disagree with it — the two-engine method is structurally blind to 63-102, which is 45% of the corpus. LSJ cannot arbitrate acute against grave either, since that is positional (Smyth §154) and not lexical. What found it was the corpus disagreeing with itself, the same test that settled the ἁλ- family and fragment 596.
